## Social caption — a Roath weekend find

Suggested use this week after access is verified; retire before Saturday 19 September 12:30. No ready queue entry.

A little detective outing in Roath this weekend 🧡

St Margaret’s Church on Waterloo Road is opening for free on Saturday 19 September, 12.30–5.30pm, and Sunday 20 September, 2–5.30pm.

There’s a children’s quiz trail to follow and colourful details to spot inside. No booking needed. We’d pick it for curious children around 5–12 with a grown-up; that’s our suggested fit, not an organiser age limit.

One important detail: the tower climb is for adults only, so this is a church-and-quiz plan for children. The church has accessible entry through its porch.

## Friday social roundup — DRAFT

Target Friday 18 September 15:30 UK after rechecking. Retire before Sat 19 September 10:00.

Cardiff: four ideas for 19–20 September, without a big ticket bill 🧡

• Penylan LEGO: Saturday 10–11am, free drop-in, ages 2+. A regular timetable session—confirm it’s running.
• St Margaret’s, Roath: free children’s quiz trail during Open Doors, Saturday 12.30–5.30pm or Sunday 2–5.30pm. No booking; tower access is adults only.
• National Museum Cardiff: dinosaurs and mammoths indoors, both days 10am–5pm; galleries close 4.45pm. Free general admission; optional day-ticket booking and paid extras separate. Parking £6.50.
• Bute Park: a self-led wooden-animal hunt. Look for the frog near Old Man’s Wood or beetle behind Summerhouse. Free park entry; use daylight hours and check gate signs.

Children with a grown-up throughout. LEGO starts at 2+; the quiz is our pick for roughly 5–12. Museum and park stops can be kept short for younger children.

Sources: cardiffhubs.co.uk/hub-events/clwb-lego/; cadw.gov.wales/open-doors-st-margarets-church-roath; museum.wales/cardiff/visit/; bute-park.com/attraction/sculpture-trail/

## Friday weekend-brief email — UNSENT

Subject: Cardiff: a Roath quiz trail, LEGO and two easy fallbacks

Preheader: Your small shortlist for 19–20 September.

Hi Cardiff,

For something a little different, try [St Margaret’s Open Doors](https://cadw.gov.wales/open-doors-st-margarets-church-roath) in Roath: Saturday 12.30–5.30pm or Sunday 2–5.30pm. The children’s quiz trail is free, no booking; the tower is adults only. Our suggested fit is curious 5–12s.

For a short Saturday morning, [Penylan’s LEGO club](https://cardiffhubs.co.uk/hub-events/clwb-lego/) lists 10–11am, free drop-in for ages 2+. Confirm the regular session before travelling.

If you need indoors, [National Museum Cardiff](https://museum.wales/cardiff/visit/) opens both days 10am–5pm, with galleries closing at 4.45pm. General entry is free; free day tickets can be booked in advance. Parking is £6.50 and paid exhibitions are separate. The dinosaur and mammoth galleries make a good starting point.

For fresh air, make your own short [Bute Park sculpture hunt](https://bute-park.com/attraction/sculpture-trail/). Ordinary park entry is free; check closing signs and stay with children beside shared paths and water.

One plan is enough. Take a grown-up, a snack and leave room to change your mind.

## Weekday subscriber email — UNSENT

Intended Monday 14 September; retire before Friday 18 September 10:30. No send configured.

Subject: Cardiff: wooden animals, real fossils and Friday rhymes

Preheader: Three manageable outings for the week ahead.

Hi Cardiff,

Make a short [Bute Park animal hunt](https://bute-park.com/attraction/sculpture-trail/): can your child find the wooden frog and beetle? It’s our own self-led idea, not an organised session. The park is free and opens at 7.30am; check the gate signs for closing time. Good for a little-leg wander or an after-school stretch.

For an indoor alternative from Tuesday 15 September, try the [Evolution of Wales galleries](https://museum.wales/cardiff/about/) at National Museum Cardiff. General entry is free. [Hours and access](https://museum.wales/cardiff/visit/): 10am–5pm, galleries close 4.45pm; closed Mondays. Under-16s need an adult. Optional advance free day ticket; parking £6.50.

For under-5s, [Rhydypennau’s English story and rhyme session](https://cardiffhubs.co.uk/hub-events/story-and-rhyme-time-english/) is listed for Friday 18 September, 10.30–11.15am. Free, no booking; confirm this weekly session before travelling.
